# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 41 (Bi-Vb Pc41)

**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc41  
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 41  
**Title (English, from literature):** Visiting places of pleasure  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Rājāgāra-sikkhāpada* ("Visiting places of pleasure", Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 41) establishes a rule of expiation (*pācittiya*) for any nun who goes to view recreational or leisure sites [Roth 1997]. The promulgated rule stipulates that an offense of expiation is committed if a nun goes to see a king's pleasure house (*rājāgāra*), a picture gallery (*cittāgāra*), a park (*ārāma*), a pleasure grove (*uyyāna*), or a lotus pond (*pokkharaṇī*) [Roth 1997]. In the rule's origin narrative, the group of six nuns visits a picture gallery inside a pleasure park (*uyyāne cittāgāre*), although the formal precept was formulated to encompass the wider list of pleasure grounds [Hüsken 1997]. Hüsken notes that this rule serves as a specific monastic restraint for nuns regarding contemporary worldly amusements and lacks a direct counterpart in the Bhikkhu Vinaya [Hüsken 1997].

 An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
